title: Core-FP8 expert bytes and FP8 projections checked against K3.25-v1; CuteAFD source audit
question: Are the Core-FP8 checkpoint's bytes what its provenance says relative to K3.25-v1, and does CuteAFD v3.0.1 share, in source, the vLLM-engine issues D1-D7 and E1 found in earlier evaluation?
engines: CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f), source read only, not run; sparkinfer submodule d3c13652

goals.question: Are the base tensors of the Core-FP8 checkpoint d31ebc92 byte-identical to the local K3.25-v1 0490d2f7 snapshot, as Core-FP8's stitch provenance records?

design.instrument: bytecheck.py: sha256 of the raw bytes of every tensor in the local K3.25-v1 snapshot, compared with Core-FP8's published stitch provenance (provenance-d31ebc92.json, not copied here)
design.items: every tensor of the 18 local shards (150,226 tensors) against the 150,405 provenance entries

goals.headline: 150,047 of 150,047 base tensors byte-identical (140.9 GB), 0 mismatches, 0 missing; 358 tensors come from the FP8 source (the 179 replaced weights and their block scales).

goals.question: For the 179 projection tensors Core-FP8 replaced, how far is the official FP8 from K3.25-v1's BF16, and does a plain E4M3 amax/448 128x128 block quantization of the BF16 reproduce the official FP8 bytes?

design.instrument: fp8check.py (CPU): dequantize official FP8 (E4M3 x FP32 128x128 block scale_inv) and compare with BF16; quantize BF16 to E4M3 with amax/448 128x128 block scales and compare codes and scales
arms: own E4M3 quantization of the BF16

goals.headline: Official FP8, dequantized, differs from K3.25-v1's BF16 by 0.16% (relative Frobenius norm, all 179 tensors). Quantizing the BF16 to E4M3 with amax/448 scales over 128x128 blocks reproduces 99.99998% of the official codes, with scales within one FP32 ulp (only 37.2% bit-equal).

goals.question: Which CuteAFD v3.0.1 code paths serve 2 RTX GPUs with local experts and no Sparks (attention placement and DSA index cache)?

design.instrument: read-only source reading of CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f) and the pinned sparkinfer submodule (d3c13652), plus the local K3.25 config.json and safetensors headers; no GPU, nothing run
design.items: placement selection and index-cache variant in the loader, daemon and launcher

goals.headline: From source: `context` (token-split MLA, compact index cache) is the automatic placement on two GPUs; `heads` (per-token key cache) is explicit and is what the v3 2-RTX release card used; both index-cache variants were read, the `layers` placement was not audited separately.

goals.question: Does CuteAFD v3.0.1 keep all 512 selected index pools (the vLLM-engine issue D1 dropped column 511)?

design.instrument: read-only source reading of CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f) and the pinned sparkinfer submodule (d3c13652), plus the local K3.25 config.json and safetensors headers; no GPU, nothing run
design.items: the CuteAFD counterpart of issue D1

goals.headline: Handled correctly (from source): all 512 selected pools are expanded, plus the open tail pool, into a 2,112-slot row on every path read; rows of exactly 512 pools take the dense branch. Not audited: whether the b12x top-k kernel's selected set is exact.

goals.question: Does CuteAFD v3.0.1 have a counterpart of the vLLM-engine issue D2 (index tail ring written without positions)?

design.instrument: read-only source reading of CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f) and the pinned sparkinfer submodule (d3c13652), plus the local K3.25 config.json and safetensors headers; no GPU, nothing run
design.items: the CuteAFD counterpart of issue D2

goals.headline: Not applicable (different design), from source: no tail ring or generic mapping fallback; every slot is addressed from the row's own position and sequence pages, and a position outside them is an error.

goals.question: Are router logits computed in FP32 in CuteAFD v3.0.1 (the vLLM-engine issue D3 computed them in BF16 on SM12x)?

design.instrument: read-only source reading of CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f) and the pinned sparkinfer submodule (d3c13652), plus the local K3.25 config.json and safetensors headers; no GPU, nothing run
design.items: the CuteAFD counterpart of issue D3

goals.headline: Handled correctly (from source): BF16 operands, FP32 accumulation and FP32 store on both GEMM routes, bias and selection in FP32; `moe_router_dtype` is not read (FP32 is unconditional). No numerical comparison was run.

goals.question: Does the routed SwiGLU limit reach CuteAFD v3.0.1's compiled expert kernels (the vLLM-engine issue D4 did not pass it)?

design.instrument: read-only source reading of CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f) and the pinned sparkinfer submodule (d3c13652), plus the local K3.25 config.json and safetensors headers; no GPU, nothing run
design.items: the CuteAFD counterpart of issue D4

goals.headline: Handled correctly (from source) for local EXL3 routed experts: compiled at 10 and enforced at startup; shared and dense MLPs also clamp at 10. Not read: the clamp inside b12x mixed_trellis; whether activations reach 10 was not measured.

goals.question: Can a CuteAFD v3.0.1 workspace referenced by a captured CUDA graph be reallocated (the vLLM-engine issue D5: workspace not locked after capture)?

design.instrument: read-only source reading of CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f) and the pinned sparkinfer submodule (d3c13652), plus the local K3.25 config.json and safetensors headers; no GPU, nothing run
design.items: the CuteAFD counterpart of issue D5

goals.headline: Not applicable (different design), from source: fixed-capacity step workspaces allocated before capture and never replaced; no resize path found in glm5_flash/engine.rs and the drafter. Not exhaustive: EXL3 shared arenas, peer-exchange buffers and token I/O were not audited.

goals.question: Can stale warm-up block ids reach CuteAFD v3.0.1's tables (the vLLM-engine issue D6)?

design.instrument: read-only source reading of CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f) and the pinned sparkinfer submodule (d3c13652), plus the local K3.25 config.json and safetensors headers; no GPU, nothing run
design.items: the CuteAFD counterpart of issue D6

goals.headline: Not applicable (different design), from source: tables are rebuilt every step, padding and warm-up rows carry -1 slots that writers skip, and per-sequence state is reset or restored before use.

goals.question: Does CuteAFD v3.0.1's index-K prefill writer handle chunk starts that are not pool-aligned (the vLLM-engine issue D7)?

design.instrument: read-only source reading of CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f) and the pinned sparkinfer submodule (d3c13652), plus the local K3.25 config.json and safetensors headers; no GPU, nothing run
design.items: the CuteAFD counterpart of issue D7

goals.headline: Handled correctly (from source) in both index caches: a straddling pool reads the sequence's own stored keys (keys cache) or its own tail (compact cache), never other sequences' rows.

goals.question: Do CuteAFD v3.0.1's router weights or logits depend on batch size (the vLLM observation E1)?

design.instrument: read-only source reading of CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f) and the pinned sparkinfer submodule (d3c13652), plus the local K3.25 config.json and safetensors headers; no GPU, nothing run
design.items: the CuteAFD counterpart of issue E1

goals.status_note: Source verdict left the route-switch logit question open; the measurement is a separate exploratory run.
goals.headline: The E1 mechanism ((s+b)-b rebuild above 1,024 rows) is not applicable (different design). Whether router logits are bit-identical across the 160/161-row GEMV/GEMM route switch cannot be determined from source; it was measured afterwards in 2026-10-26-e1-router-route.

goals.question: Which of CuteAFD v3.0.1's MLP clamps and related keys are read from the checkpoint's config.json?

design.instrument: read-only source reading of CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f) and the pinned sparkinfer submodule (d3c13652), plus the local K3.25 config.json and safetensors headers; no GPU, nothing run
design.items: every consumer of swiglu_limit and related router keys

goals.headline: From source: routed experts, shared expert and dense MLPs clamp at 10 from compiled constants; none read `swiglu_limit` from config.json, and no equality check was found, so a checkpoint declaring another value would not be detected (the local K3.25 declares 10.0). `routed_scaling_factor`, `index_topk` and `index_kpool` are read; `moe_router_dtype` is not.

goals.question: What did the source audit not cover?

design.instrument: read-only source reading of CuteAFD v3.0.1 (commit 9098781f) and the pinned sparkinfer submodule (d3c13652), plus the local K3.25 config.json and safetensors headers; no GPU, nothing run

goals.headline: Source only, no behaviour measured, released image not inspected; submodule read at the pinned commit without verifying the image was built from it; b12x internals, FP8/NVFP4 local expert paths, Spark worker paths and the `layers` placement not read.
